doc.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022

title: Technology and hooking young students on jazz
summary: He cites Randy Brecker's pedals, TikTok and sampling, and teaching by making students aware of jazz roots and playing transcribed tunes like Song for My Father.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: If jazz is dead why are there still great schools like Berklee and North Texas State and Miami and whoever else I forgot to mention. Okay? These educational institutions aren’t just bringing in students under some kind of a false pretense. The other thing of course is the technological aspect of it plays a really, really, really big role. I’ll give you a good example. Before the Covid I went to see Randy Brecker, who is a dear friend, over at the resurrected My Father’s Place. And the feature artist there, it was Billy Cobham’s group. And they were literally re-living these great Billy Cobham albums that Billy did with Randy, with Michael, God rest his soul, and Paul Hansen, the bassoonist played Michael’s parts. Okay. And you know he’s a great, great, great jazz bassoonist. I mean he’s a monster. But here’s my point about the technical. So Randy is playing and he’s incorporating you know all of these foot pedals, you know that look like Sam Ash’s electronics. There’s this one, this one, this one, this one, this one, but of course being the great musician that he is he’s using them in a very, very wise way. Point number one. Point number two, you have YouTube, TikTok, in-home studio, in-home video you know, literally anyone can incorporate recording video and audio and present it. So I have young students or new students when I was teaching schools or what-have-you. “Are you a TikTocker?” “Yeah I’m a TikTocker, I have 900,000 you know followers.” That’s like my grandson says. He’s got like 900,000. So I said to him, “What do you TikTok about?” He says, “We TikTok about gaming” or what-have-you. So I says, “Well you ever think about TikToking about a song that you might have heard that really is kind of a re-make of a jazz song? Or a song that’s sampled from a jazz song? You know like ‘Cantaloupe Island.’” Okay? Or, oh gosh, the pop tune was “Billy Don’t Call that Number” — I forget the — they sampled another tune. But you know you say to the young student well that actually came from this here. And it goes back to that question about how come you don’t know about Charlie Parker? Well it’s our job to tell you about Charlie Parker. Okay? It’s our job to get you hooked on it. So if you’re savvy enough as an educator and willing to go the extra not even couple of yards, if you’re willing to go a couple of inches to bring the jazz experience into what the young students are doing, okay, I mean that is like the bait on the hook that catches the bass. You know? Another quick example: as I mentioned to you before I don’t like to use method books per se, you know. I like to entertain. So I write these tunes on Finale. And over the years I’ve written about 1,200 or so. Some of them are transcriptions. All right? And they’re transcriptions of a tune like “Song for my Father.” Okay? So we put that song in the — and you know I will modify the tune to make it a little bit easier with the embellishments and the trills and what-have-you, and then we’ll listen to the song after we learn it and play it. “You just played that same song, you know, that Lee Morgan played.” Okay?
